META: 1-800‑GOT‑JUNK will pick up and recycle electronics, but pricing is volume‑based (≈$100‑$1,100) and free alternatives often beat the cost. 
KEYWORDS: 1-800‑got‑junk electronics recycling, e‑waste disposal cost, junk removal pricing, free e‑waste programs, junk removal vs DIY 

# 1-800-GOT-JUNK for Electronics Recycling 

**Yes, 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK will haul your TVs, computers, phones and other e‑waste, but you’ll pay a volume‑based fee that can range from $100 to $1,099 per load.** Below is everything you need to know before you call, from exact pricing to what happens to your devices after they leave your driveway. 

--- 

## How 1-800‑GOT‑JUNK Pricing Works 

### Volume‑Based Pricing (the only numbers you’ll see) 

| Load Size | Approx. Dimensions | Price Range* |
|-----------|-------------------|--------------|
| Minimum (1/8 truck) | 1.25 ft L × 5 ft H × 8 ft W | **$100 – $150** |
| Small load | up to 1/8‑truck volume | **$107 – $396** |
| Medium load | roughly 1/4‑truck | **$396 – $600** |
| Large load | up to 1/2‑truck | **$600 – $1,099** |
| Half truck | 5 ft L × 5 ft H × 8 ft W | **$400 – $600** |
| Full truck | 10 ft L × 5 ft H × 8 ft W (≈ 18 cu yd) | **$600 – $1,000** |

\*Ranges reflect the full national spread; most mid‑size metros land near the middle of each band. 

The **average job across all customers is about $240**, which is a useful benchmark if you’re not sure how much space your junk will occupy. 

### What’s Included 

* All labor (no need to move items to the curb) 
* Loading from anywhere on your property 
* Hauling, disposal, and recycling fees 
* Post‑service cleanup (crew sweeps the area) 
* Fully licensed and insured crews 

No hidden “dump” fees appear after the crew leaves. 

### Booking Process – No Surprise Quotes 

1. **Call 1‑800‑468‑5865 or book online.** 
2. The franchise schedules a **free on‑site estimate**; no credit card is required. 
3. The crew calls **25–30 minutes before arrival**. Same‑day service is often available. 
4. If you prefer a DIY bag or container, the “Flex” product lets you **load it yourself** and the crew picks it up for a flat **$39** fee (price shown online). 

> **No price is given over the phone or on the website**; the estimate is always done in person. 

--- 

## What Happens to Your Electronics? 

### Certified Recycling Partners 

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK works only with **R2 and e‑Stewards certified recyclers**. These programs require third‑party audits that confirm hazardous metals, plastics and rare earths are **properly recovered** and not dumped in a landfill. 

### Data Destruction 

* **Hard drives and SSDs** are either **physically shredded** or **de‑gaussed** before entering the recycling stream. 
* For laptops, tablets and phones, the crew **removes batteries** (which are sent to a separate hazardous‑waste facility) and then the remaining chassis go to the certified recycler. 

### Materials Recovered vs. Landfilled 

| Material | Typical Recovery Rate* |
|----------|------------------------|
| Copper (wiring, circuit boards) | **≈ 30 %** |
| Aluminum (frames, heat sinks) | **≈ 20 %** |
| Plastics (casings, cables) | **≈ 15 %** |
| Precious metals (gold, palladium) | **< 1 %** |
| Residual waste (non‑recyclable) | **≈ 34 %** |

\*Numbers are industry averages from R2/e‑Stewards reports; the exact split varies by device mix. 

--- 

## State Regulations and What You Can’t Toss 

### Federal & State E‑Waste Laws 

* **U.S. EPA** classifies many electronics as **hazardous waste** because of lead, mercury, cadmium and brominated flame retardants. 
* **California, New York, Massachusetts, Washington and a handful of other states** require **special permits** for disposal; most junk‑removal firms, including 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK, have those permits. 

### Items Typically Excluded from General Junk Removal 

| Item | Why It May Be Excluded |
|------|------------------------|
| CRT televisions | Heavy leaded glass; many franchises charge extra handling fees. |
| Large server racks | Often require specialized disassembly and data‑destruction services. |
| Lithium‑ion batteries | Treated as hazardous; must be separated and sent to a certified recycler. |
| Fluorescent light fixtures | Contain mercury; separate collection is required by law. |

If a franchise refuses an item, they will **tell you on the spot** and may suggest a local hazardous‑waste drop‑off instead. 

--- 

## Free and Low‑Cost Alternatives 

### Manufacturer Take‑Back Programs 

* **Apple, Dell, HP, Samsung** and many other OEMs run **mail‑in or store‑drop programs** for old devices, often at **no cost**. 
* Some manufacturers even **pay you a small credit** (e.g., Apple’s Trade‑In) if the device is in working condition. 

### Retail Drop‑Off 

| Retailer | Accepted Items | Hours / Restrictions |
|----------|----------------|----------------------|
| **Best Buy** | TVs, monitors, laptops, phones, small appliances | 7 days/week; no appointment needed |
| **Staples** | Computers, printers, keyboards, small electronics | Same‑day drop‑off; limited to 20 items per visit |
| **Home Depot** (selected stores) | Small e‑waste, batteries | Often tied to local recycling events |

These programs are **free** and usually faster than scheduling a full‑truck pickup. 

### Municipal Collection Days 

Most cities hold **annual or semi‑annual e‑waste collection events**. Check your city’s website for dates; they typically accept **all electronics** (including CRTs) at **no charge**. 

> **Bottom line:** If you have only a few items (under a half‑truck load) and a free drop‑off is available nearby, that option almost always beats a $100‑$400 pickup fee. 

--- 

## Comparing the Competition 

| Company | Minimum Charge | Pricing Model | Typical Full‑Truck Range | Coverage | Notable Feature |
|---------|----------------|---------------|--------------------------|----------|-----------------|
| **1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK** | **$100 – $150** (1/8 truck) | Volume‑based (truck size) | **$600 – $1,000** | U.S. (all 50 states) | Licensed crews, all‑inclusive price |
| **LoadUp** | **$89** (per item) | Per‑item flat rate, online guarantee | N/A (item‑based) | All 50 states | Instant online pricing, price never changes on service day |
| **Junk King** | **$99** (minimum) | Volume‑based | **$589 – $658** (full truck) | Gaps in several states | Approximate online estimate, confirmed on site |
| **College Hunks Hauling Junk** | **$150 – $750** (per job) | Volume‑based | N/A | Nationwide | $99 dispatch fee often added after booking |

**When is 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK the better choice?** 
* You need **full‑service loading** (no curb‑side loading) and want **all labor, disposal and cleanup bundled**. 
* Your load is **large enough** to fill a half‑truck or more, making the per‑item cost of LoadUp higher than the $400‑$600 range of a half‑truck. 

**When is a competitor or free option smarter?** 
* You have **few items** (< 5 medium electronics). LoadUp’s per‑item pricing may be under **$200 total**. 
* You can drive to a **Best Buy or municipal drop‑off**; that is $0. 

--- 

## Worked Example – Calculating Your 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK Bill 

Assume a suburban household wants to discard the following: 

* 55‑in CRT TV (≈ 12 cu ft) 
* 24‑in flat‑panel TV (≈ 5 cu ft) 
* Desktop computer with monitor (≈ 8 cu ft) 
* Laptop (≈ 2 cu ft) 
* Printer (≈ 1 cu ft) 
* Small sofa (≈ 15 cu ft) 

**Step 1 – Add volumes** 
12 + 5 + 8 + 2 + 1 + 15 = **43 cu ft** 

**Step 2 – Convert to truck size** 
* Minimum load (1/8 truck) ≈ 6 cu ft (1.25 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft) 
* Half‑truck ≈ 30 cu ft (5 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft) 

43 cu ft exceeds a half‑truck, so the crew will need a **large/near‑full load**. 

**Step 3 – Apply pricing range** 
Large load: **$600 – $1,099**. 

If the franchise assesses the job at the **mid‑range ($850)**, that’s the final price. 

**Step 4 – Compare to alternatives** 

* **LoadUp**: 6 items × $89 = $534 (price locked online). 
* **Best Buy drop‑off**: $0 (if you can transport the sofa). 

In this scenario, **LoadUp saves roughly $300** and a free drop‑off saves **the entire $850**—but only if you can move the sofa yourself. 

--- 

## Common Mistakes When Using Junk Removal Services 

* **Assuming “all‑inclusive” means “free disposal.”** The price already covers disposal, but you still pay the volume fee. 
* **Not pre‑sorting** – crews charge the same for a half‑truck whether it’s 30 cu ft of cardboard or 30 cu ft of heavy electronics. 
* **Over‑booking multiple pickups** – splitting a load into two trips doubles labor and travel costs. 
* **Believing coupon codes work** – most aggregator codes are **expired or invalid**; the only reliable discount is the **$10‑$25 email‑list coupon**. 
* **Skipping free local programs** – many cities accept CRTs and large appliances for free; ignoring them can waste $100‑$400. 

--- 

## FAQ 

**Q1. Does 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK recycle electronics or just dump them?** 
Yes. All electronics are sent to **R2/e‑Stewards certified recyclers**, where hazardous components are removed and valuable metals are recovered. 

**Q2. How do I know what size truck I need?** 
The on‑site estimate will measure your load and suggest the smallest truck that fits. The **average job is $240**, which usually corresponds to a small‑to‑medium load (≈ 15‑30 cu ft). 

**Q3. Are there any hidden fees for batteries or data destruction?** 
No. Battery removal, data shredding and hazardous‑waste handling are **included in the quoted price**. 

**Q4. Can I get a discount for being a veteran or senior?** 
There is **NO official military, senior, student, or AAA discount**. The only guaranteed savings are the **email‑list coupons** and local franchise promotions. 

**Q5. What if my city has a strict e‑waste law?** 
1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK’s franchise will **comply with local regulations**; if an item is prohibited, the crew will advise you to use a municipal drop‑off instead. 

**Q6. Should I choose LoadUp over 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK for a small job?** 
If you have **fewer than 5 items** and can handle curb‑side loading, LoadUp’s **per‑item pricing (starting at $89)** often ends up cheaper than the $100‑$150 minimum for a 1/8‑truck load.

## Bottom‑Line Takeaway 

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK will pick up and properly recycle your electronics, but **price is driven by volume**, not by item count. For a **single TV or laptop**, free alternatives (manufacturer take‑back, Best Buy drop‑off, or municipal e‑waste days) almost always beat the $100‑$400 pickup fee. If you have a **large, mixed load** that you cannot move yourself, the **all‑inclusive service** (including data destruction and cleanup) can be worth the cost—especially when you consolidate everything into one truck and take advantage of the **email‑list discount**.
